messages:
sylvie: heads-up — after the us-west rolling node update I’m seeing ~40 pods stuck in Pending in batch/priority-batch. Fit failure is all 'Insufficient GPUs' even though we just added capacity to the gpu-slice pool.

nate: can you paste the `kubectl describe` for one of the pending pods? also which nodepool was scaled?

sylvie: here — truncated:
```
Events:
  Type     Reason            Age    From               Message
  ----     ------            ----   ----               -------
  Normal   Scheduled         3m     default-scheduler  Successfully assigned batch/job-xyz to gpu-node-14
  Warning  FailedScheduling  3m     kube-scheduler     0/18 nodes are available: 18 Insufficient redwood.com/gpu-slice.
```
Pod Resources:
  requests:
    cpu: 2000m
    memory: 8Gi
    redwood.com/gpu-slice: 0.5
```

sylvie: node labels show gpu-slice capacity present. nodes report allocatable but scheduler still rejects. :face_with_raised_eyebrow:

alex: two quick hypotheses: 1) device-plugin registered resource name mismatch (we moved from `redwood.com/gpu-slice` -> `redwood.com/slice-gpu` in the nodepool image) 2) autoscaler creating nodes but they stay NotReady long enough and scheduler counts them as available incorrectly.

ops-elena: I also saw several CNI errors during the kubelet restart on the new image: `Failed to create pod network: CNI failed to allocate` — network attach delay ~45s which means nodes were Ready only after TTL we set for autoscaler (60s). autoscaler-bot logs show nodes removed from scale-up consideration because of `ready=false` within 30s window.

k8s-autoscaler-bot: scale-up event suppressed: new nodes marked NotReady for 48s; cluster-autoscaler: node group gpu-slice-pool reached max size? (cur=8,max=8)
\
deploy-bot: infra:us-west1/gpu-slice-pool bumped from 6->8 at 1995012200 (spot).

nate: ok that explains spot cap, but the Insufficient resource still sounds like resource name mismatch. sylvie, can you `kubectl get nodes -o jsonpath` the resource list for one of the new nodes?

sylvie: pasted:
```
kubectl get node gpu-node-14 -o jsonpath='{.status.allocatable}'
{cpu: "32", memory: "120Gi", "redwood.com/gpu-slice": "4"}
```

nate: uh — that shows `redwood.com/gpu-slice` present. so not mismatch. Next: are the pods requesting fractional with float 0.5? device plugin may require integer milli-slices (e.g., 500m). what does the pod spec show?

sylvie: snippet from podspec:
```
resources:
  requests:
    redwood.com/gpu-slice: "0.5"
```

alex: there's the thing — our device plugin only accepts integer milli units (it registers `redwood.com/gpu-slice-milli` and the scheduler plugin translates. older scheduler path handled float but kube's scheduler sees it as string and fails to match. Some pods from the job were created before we rolled the device plugin so they used old resource name; mixed resource names + decimals are causing binpack holes.

ops-elena: action items: 1) add admission webhook to normalize requests to `redwood.com/gpu-slice-milli` 2) backfill node labels for legacy resources 3) bump gpu-slice-pool max to 12 temporarily while we fix admission so jobs don't backlog. also consider increasing cluster-autoscaler `--scale-up-unneeded-time` to 90s to tolerate CNI delays.

nate: agree. quick mitigation: we can add a PodPreset (or mutating webhook) to convert `redwood.com/gpu-slice: "0.5"` -> `redwood.com/gpu-slice-milli: "500"` so scheduler can binpack. I'll spin a PoC.

sylvie: thanks. also we should audit all nodepools for mixed device-plugin versions — I found two pools (gpu-slice-pool and gpu-slice-burst) with slightly different plugin images which explains the mixed resource names.

alex: long term: consider switching to explicit packing policy for these batch jobs (preferPacked topology) + consolidate to single device-plugin version, OR move to MIG-backed exclusive-resource model to avoid fractional complexity. MIG reduces fragmentation but increases cost if we overprovision.

ops-elena: noted in infra-runbook: update autoscaler max for gpu-slice-pool, add post-rolling check for CNI readiness (wait for `kubelet.networkReady`), and file ticket to add admission webhook.

sylvie: i'll open the infra PR for scaling limits and create the admission webhook ticket. I'll also trigger a temporary manual scale to 12 to drain the queue.

nate: thanks — ping here when POC mutating webhook is up and we can close the backlog.

alex: small follow-up — cost note: bumping pool max with spots will increase transient spend + preemption risk. if backlog persists we should evaluate shifting some jobs to dedicated reserved nodes during high batch windows.

sylvie: understood, will attach cost estimate to the PR. :thumbsup:
